SHW.rationale: Sherwin-Williams is the global #1 coatings company with a durable competitive moat (5,000+ company-operated stores, contractor loyalty, pricing power) and a GF Score of 91/100. Q1 2026 showed solid YoY growth: revenue +6.8%, EPS +7.5%, with all segments contributing. However, the picture is more nuanced than headline numbers suggest. QoQ trends are sharply negative (revenue -10.9%, EPS -35.8%) reflecting seasonal softness but also the magnitude of the Q1 operating cash flow collapse (-327.7% YoY to $139M) and the fact that Q1 is structurally weak. The company carries significant leverage ($9.3B debt, D/E 2.1x) and the balance sheet shows total equity of only $4.4B against $26.4B in assets. Valuation at 29x P/E is at the low end of its 365-day range (28.5-37.1), suggesting some de-rating has occurred, but it is not cheap in absolute terms for a company guiding low-to-mid single-digit sales growth with housing headwinds persisting. The company reaffirmed FY2026 EPS guidance of $10.70-$11.10 (adjusted $11.50-$11.90), implying ~4-5% growth at midpoint. Management is executing disciplined capital returns ($773M to shareholders in Q1 alone) and the 47-year dividend increase streak is intact. Near-term catalysts are limited: no major earnings event until Q2 results in late July, and management explicitly noted 'little to no recovery in most end markets this year.' The stock is down 15.4% over the past quarter, which has brought valuation toward the lower end of its range, but the fundamental trajectory is modest rather than compelling. Net margin has compressed slightly (10.9% vs 11.6% a year ago). The score reflects a high-quality franchise at a more reasonable but not bargain valuation, with a modestly positive but unspectacular near-term trajectory and no immediate re-rating catalyst.
